video_title: Dwyane Wade & Udonis Haslem Answer Everything Fans Want to Know

quotes.speaker: Udonis Haslem
quotes.summary_phrase: Udonis Haslem's advice on not letting people cheat you
quotes.excerpt: Don't ever let nobody cheat you or take what you deserve.
quotes.quote: I cannot really say it was about basketball, but it was about life, and I applied it to sports: don't ever let nobody cheat you or take what you deserve. I got that from my pops. I remember catching a bus to go see my mom, and I went to pay for a bus ticket, and my change was short. It was only two dollars, but I did not feel like getting back in the long line for two dollars. I got back to that car and I was two dollars short, my daddy went to the fuck off. Don't you ever let nobody cheat you for what you deserve, what you work for, what you earn. Get your ass back in line and go get your two dollars. I applied that in everything that I did when it came to sports. If I worked for it and I deserve it, I am not going to let you take it from me.

quotes.speaker: Dwyane Wade
quotes.summary_phrase: Dwyane Wade on the importance of developing his left hand
quotes.excerpt: My dad made me work on my left hand just as much as I worked on my right.
quotes.quote: I am a right-hand basketball player. Work on your left hand and make your left hand just as good as your right hand. My dad always told me that. He did not want me to be a player that you had to push me one direction or I had to finish one direction. He wanted me to be versatile, that I could do anything on the floor and feel comfortable on either side of the floor. My dad made me work on my left hand just as much as I worked on my right hand. If you seen me play, especially early in my career, I can turn and get in that paint and I go with that left. It is like Kyrie. When you watch Kyrie get down in certain areas, that left is just as good as that right.

quotes.speaker: Dwyane Wade
quotes.summary_phrase: Dwyane Wade on never letting opponents punk him
quotes.excerpt: You better always stand up for yourself and do not never let nobody punk you.
quotes.quote: Do not let anyone punk you. When you are playing this game of basketball, and if you are going to be a good basketball player, you are going to have people who will try to punk you because they are bigger than you, because they are older than you, because they feel like they are tougher than you. You better always stand up for yourself and do not never let nobody punk you. I never let nobody punk me or take me out of my game. The physicality that they try to present to me and use on me, you will not punk me, dog.

quotes.speaker: Udonis Haslem
quotes.summary_phrase: Udonis Haslem on the outdated 'finish your food' culture
quotes.excerpt: I do not make my kids finish their food anymore.
quotes.quote: We grew up in a society where if you did not have much money, you were taught to always finish your food. Your parents always made you finish your food regardless of what the hell was going on. I used to see that at the table, my grits get cold and my mama made me cut them like cake. I had to finish that shit. I do not make my kids finish their food anymore. If you are full, push that shit to the side or throw it away. I do not make my kids finish their food anymore. So the finish your food culture, those days of finishing your food, I do not agree with that. Eat until you are full and throw that shit away and you will get some more later.

quotes.speaker: Udonis Haslem
quotes.summary_phrase: Udonis Haslem's simple two-meal-a-day diet plan
quotes.excerpt: I start with fruit and I only eat twice a day.
quotes.quote: I start with fruit and I only eat twice a day. I do not eat no red meat, I do not eat pork, I do not eat beef. So whatever my meal today will be, I start with fruit in the morning and throughout the day it will be something. My first meal will probably be protein heavy, chicken or something like that with a carb, a pasta or a rice. And then the night, I will figure it out. But for the most part, I only eat twice a day with a fruit to start my day in the morning and I might have a shake. So those are my days, it is fruit, shake and two meals.

quotes.speaker: Dwyane Wade
quotes.summary_phrase: Dwyane Wade on his daily supplement and recovery routine
quotes.excerpt: I start my day with collagen and magnesium.
quotes.quote: I start my day with what I call my daily supplements. I start with my protein shake, and in my protein shake, that is where I get all the things that I need. We are getting older now, and so I am looking at things like my joints, my bone joints, my liver. I am looking at how can I supplement these things in my body because I am sure I am not getting anything. I am looking at healthy aging. I have all these products that is put inside my protein shake, creatine, daily greens. I start my morning with collagen and magnesium. Magnesium is one of the greatest things for your mind. I start with testosterone support, I am getting older, I take my pills in the morning, dog.

quotes.speaker: Udonis Haslem
quotes.summary_phrase: Udonis Haslem on Shaq trying to fight Dwyane Wade
quotes.excerpt: When Shaq tried to fight Dwyane Wade, butt-ass naked, and I had to break that shit up.

text_blocks.speaker: Udonis Haslem
text_blocks.text: When Shaq tried to fight Dwyane Wade, butt-ass naked, and I had to break that shit up. I am like, hold on big fella, what are we doing? Like, what are we doing? Like we butt-ass naked, like you are going to fight right now? Like come on big fella, do not make me have to break this one up. As a captain, I get it, I am the captain, but I do not want this job, not today. Not today. Not today. I do not want to be captain no more.

text_blocks.speaker: Dwyane Wade
text_blocks.text: That one right there is an all-time. If I got to go with one that is not as dramatic as two grown men in the shower about to fight, I am going to go with a time where Eddie Jones had Jerome Beasley's linen suit hung up in the middle of the locker room when we walked in.

quotes.speaker: Udonis Haslem
quotes.summary_phrase: Udonis Haslem on his Lisfranc injury ending his prime
quotes.excerpt: For me it is when I had the Lisfranc injury.
quotes.quote: For me it is when I had the Lisfranc injury, when I tore my third, fourth and fifth metatarsal. First of all, I came back at the end of that season and I played in the playoffs, and we lost to Dallas that year. Then I came back and played the next year, but in all honesty, I was not the same player for probably two years after that. It took me a year and a half to get back to the level I was at before I got hurt. But by that time my role had changed and I was in a different situation as a basketball player. So I just felt like my injury set me back a little bit and the path of my career changed.

quotes.speaker: Dwyane Wade
quotes.summary_phrase: Dwyane Wade on his 2012 knee surgery ending his prime
quotes.excerpt: I would say, very similar to Udonis, it was my third knee surgery. It was in 2012.
quotes.quote: I would say, very similar to Udonis, it was my third knee surgery. It was in 2012. So after we beat OKC in the finals in 2012, that summer I got my third knee surgery, and after that I do not feel like I never got back my explosion. Maybe I came back a little too quick. We went to the finals and I got knee surgery and I was there for training camp the next year. Maybe I came back a little too quick for my third knee surgery and I did not get myself really a full time to really heal. And I never got back, like when I was driving to the bucket, I can see that I could not take off like I used to.

quotes.speaker: Udonis Haslem
quotes.summary_phrase: Udonis Haslem on the NBA's 'new shiny toy' syndrome
quotes.excerpt: The NBA is like new shiny toy syndrome. They get a new shiny toy, but they forget.
quotes.quote: The NBA is like new shiny toy syndrome. They get a new shiny toy, but they forget about that old toy fast. I did, to the grace of God, get back to the level that I thought I needed to be at, but then it was a whole different set of circumstances I was dealing with as a basketball player. This game passes you by, man. You get great players coming into these organizations, and you fuck around and you hurt for a year and a half, two years, and you are not your best version, there is another young motherfucker coming in and can play and those opportunities got to go to other people. So the NBA is like new shiny toy syndrome.
